earlier_scan.source_named: Booth, Madeleine 2015. A Preliminary Sketch of Yokoim Phonology and Morphology (59pp)

sources.note: 60-item wordlist with no stress marks and no notes.

sources.citation: Telban, Borut. 1994. Dancing through time: temporality and identity in a Sepik cosmology. PhD thesis, Australian National University, 309 pp. (hdl 1885/116905)
sources.note: 'Note on orthography' (p. xii, PDF p. 12) gives four vowels /a i ɨ u/, r/l and s/t allophony, ng vs ngg; nothing at all on stress or accent. Its bibliography lists 'Telban, B. in press a. The grammar of Karawari, East Sepik Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics' which never appeared.

sources.citation: Anderson, Gregory D. S., K. David Harrison & Madeleine Booth. 2014-. Yokoim Living (Talking) Dictionary. Living Tongues Institute for Endangered Languages (Swarthmore record works.swarthmore.edu/fac-linguistics/289)
sources.note: Entries (Karawari, Konmei, Kundiman, Manjamai dialects) in phonemic transcription without stress marks; Grammar and About tabs are empty ('No information yet').

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2005. Linguistic prehistory in the Sepik-Ramu basin. In Pawley, Attenborough, Golson & Hide (eds.), Papuan Pasts, 109-144. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 572 (whole-volume PDF, hdl 1885/146735)
sources.note: Comparative and classificatory; Karawari appears only in the Lower Sepik subgrouping table and pronoun/cognate sets; no statement about stress in any Lower Sepik language (the only 'stress' hits in the volume are in Pawley's Kalam/pTNG chapter).

sources.citation: Abbott, Stan. 1985. Nor-Pondo lexicostatistical survey. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22, 313-338. Pacific Linguistics A-63 (hdl 1885/254469)
sources.note: Lexicostatistical wordlist survey listing 'Karawari Language: 1,300' speakers; no phonological notes and no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25 (hdl 1885/146478)
sources.note: Entry 119 KARAWARI (Tabriak): villages, population 1300, test DCL71, cites Dye & Townsends 1969 and Haberland; no phonology.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.

sources.citation: Booth, Madeleine. 2015. A preliminary sketch of Yokoim phonology and morphology. Swarthmore College senior thesis (Linguistics), 59 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only phonological description of the language known to Glottolog; a phonology sketch of this kind normally includes a stress section. Not in Swarthmore Digital Commons or Tripod; the department's thesis pages (swarthmore.edu/linguistics) sit behind a JS challenge and no copy was found online. Ask the Swarthmore Linguistics Department, K. David Harrison, or the author.
